back: An increase in the real output of goods and services (real GDP) of an economy over time.

front: What is the difference between **nominal** and **real** GDP?
back: Nominal GDP is at current prices; real GDP is adjusted for inflation (at constant, base-year prices).
(Real GDP this year − real GDP last year) ÷ real GDP last year × 100.

front: Name four causes of economic growth.
back: Investment in capital; a larger or better-skilled labour force; new technology; discovery of natural resources; more total demand when resources are idle.

front: Give three signs of economic growth.
back: New and expanding firms; rising employment; more goods in shops; higher incomes and spending; more tax revenue.

front: Give four benefits of economic growth.
back: Higher living standards; more jobs; more tax revenue for public services; less poverty; more investment.

front: Give four costs of economic growth.
back: Pollution; depletion of non-renewable resources; wider inequality; inflation; opportunity cost of lower consumption now.

front: Can real GDP rise while real GDP per head falls?
back: Yes: if the population grows faster than real GDP.

front: If the growth rate falls from 5% to 2%, does output fall?
back: No: output still rises, only more slowly. Output falls only when growth is negative.
